## Historical audit: S0031, visible chunk 1 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/selection/commons_184317253/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. No reference or rendered image pixels are visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The explicit goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, including viewpoint, framing, materials and occlusion, without using the image as a texture. The scene’s identity and contents are **student interpretations**, not independently observed facts. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5 | The first program constructed multiple objects: walls, floor, fireplace, cabinets, door, dome, cauldron, vessels and barrier. It specified ceramic-colored polygons, procedural plaster noise and bump, wood and iron materials; separate cauldron handles and feet and cabinet parts were positioned by coordinates, not verified as connected. It set camera, lights and Cycles settings. Step 1 returned `ok: true` and saved a render and blend file. |
| Student review request, lines 6–8 | Step 1 was selected. The next student request included the original and rendered image paths and asked for comparison; the session completed with no recorded tool calls. This establishes image delivery to the student session, not what the student perceived. |
| Student revision and execution, lines 9–12 | The revised program moved the camera from `(3.10,-6.10,1.66)` to `(-3.30,-.60,1.50)`, moved the cauldron and barrier, raised the dome, made tiles denser, changed the door portal, added floor slabs and reduced lighting and exposure. Step 2 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected. |

**Validation and outcome.** Both visible builds succeeded technically. The logs report 16 render samples despite the programs requesting 48; the cause and visual effect are unknown (lines 3, 5, 9, 11). Camera framing, lighting, object placement and pose, material appearance, part contact, and reference similarity cannot be verified without the images or geometric inspection. No articulated figure or pose assessment is evidenced. Selection is not a formal quality score or proof of reconstruction correctness. The overall outcome is **unknown**, rather than formal success, partial correctness, algorithm failure, empty patch, or technical interruption; later chunks are not visible.

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher input, diagnosis, proposed update, or student adoption is visible in this chunk. The revision followed a runner-provided comparison prompt, not evidenced teacher advice. The student autonomously produced and revised code, but there is no recorded independent tool exploration in the two visible model sessions (lines 2 and 8).

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferable observation: successful execution and a saved render validate the pipeline, not visual or geometric fidelity. Task-specific choices include the tiled chamber interpretation, camera reversal and darker lighting. Whether those changes improved the match, whether parts actually touch, and whether subsequent review or submission changed the result remain unresolved.
